newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - high sulphur loses some gloss.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - high sulphur loses some gloss.

text.p: NWE cracked high sulphur fuel oil lost some of its gloss on Wednesday as barges and swaps slipped back. Low sulphur material was more solid.
Traders said physical cargoes were broadly steady but the firm tone has eased.

"Prices went too far, there was not enough fundamental support, the French strike has been overplayed," said one trader. A cracked Russian cargo of 22,000 tonnes out of Tallin was heard offered at the equivalent of about $124 cif NWE, which some dealers felt was $2 above the market.
Utility buying interest was not apparent.
"If they didn't want to buy when it was down at $110 cif, the price coming down to $120 cif is not going to entice them," said one end-user who thought buying interest was muted at best.
But some traders felt the latest buy tender from Portugal for 75,000 tonnes in December and January, won by German trader Stinnes, would help prop up the market.
"There is also the Turkish tender (for 45-50kt) that is awarded on Friday," commented a trader.
The low sulphur sector looked firmer with Dec swaps done at $135 and $135.50 fob. "U.S interest and fairly tight stocks are keeping prices firm," said one dealer. -- +44 171 542 8980
